newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Cardoso vows to push civil service reform.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Cardoso vows to push civil service reform.

text.p: Brazil's President Fernando Henrique Cardoso vowed to push on with efforts to win Congress' approval of his civil service reform bill and slammed leftist lawmakers for opposing it, an official said.
"The president will continue to fight for administrative and pension reforms," the president's chief spokesman Sergio Amaral told reporters late Wednesday.

"But he finds it strange that leftist parties, those who pretend to defend most the poor and needy, vote against a measure that aims to combat privilege and scandalous public service salaries," he added.

Cardoso suffered a stinging defeat Tuesday when the lower house watered down his bill, approving an amendment barring states and cities from setting their own pay ceilings below a $10,188 monthly cap for federal workers to cut payroll costs.
Late Wednesday, the government defeated another oppositon amendment but, fearing fresh defeats, delayed further voting on the legislation in the Chamber of Deputies until next week.
"The president laments that a minoritty in the Chamber of Deputies is blocking necessary and moral changes," Amaral said.
He quoted Cardoso as saying opposition lawmakers are preventing states from "defending their payrolls and making fiscal adjustments."
"Each one will have to take responsibility before the country and explain why they voted against a measure that would end privilege," he added.
Civil service reform is considered crucial to the government's attempts to rein in pubic spending but has run into entrenched opposition in Congress.
Many observors now believe the government may not get the legislation and another bill to reform the pension system through Congress before next year's presidential and congressional elections.
